groups.summary: Choose the circuit character and filter slope before adding saturation.

modes.name: Active
modes.choose_for: Narrower, controlled 1970s-style focus and decisive range trimming.
modes.sound: Harder, more localized shaping with 18 dB/octave cuts.
modes.watch_for: The steeper edges can sound too deliberate on broad acoustic sources.

modes.name: Passive
modes.choose_for: Wider sources and broad, glowing 1960s-style contour.
modes.sound: Softer interaction with 6 dB/octave cuts and a more acoustic-feeling spread.
modes.watch_for: Maxing both outer boosts can effectively cancel the Mid control.

modes.name: Off
modes.choose_for: Using only the independent saturation circuit.
modes.sound: No EQ or range-filter contribution; the color stage remains available.
modes.watch_for: Re-level before comparing—the missing EQ may change perceived energy.

groups.summary: The label names the spectral extreme that stays comparatively intact.

modes.name: Keep Low
modes.choose_for: Bass, kick, or full-range material whose foundation must stay firm.
modes.sound: The higher part of the signal saturates more than the low end.
modes.watch_for: It is easy to misread this as the band being distorted; it is the protected band.

modes.name: Neutral
modes.choose_for: Even full-band density without protecting either extreme.
modes.sound: All frequencies encounter the saturation more evenly.
modes.watch_for: Low end can fuzz and highs can harden together when driven too far.

modes.name: Keep High
modes.choose_for: Bright percussion or vocals whose air and articulation must survive.
modes.sound: Lower frequencies saturate more while the top stays clearer.
modes.watch_for: Too much can thicken low mids while leaving the source deceptively bright.

groups.summary: Separate lighter modern ratios from the classic hardware ratios and its famous accidental state.

modes.name: Low ratios
modes.choose_for: Gentler track control, parallel work, or 1:1 color without normal compression.
modes.sound: Less assertive gain reduction while retaining the modeled FET and transformer stages.
modes.watch_for: Drive stages can still add attitude even when the ratio is low.

modes.name: High ratios
modes.choose_for: The familiar fast, forward FET envelope on vocals, drums, bass, and guitars.
modes.sound: Classic 4:1 through 20:1-style urgency with increasingly firm peak control.
modes.watch_for: Fast attack can remove the very transient that made the source feel close.

modes.name: British
modes.choose_for: Explosive room mics, parallel drums, or deliberately unruly vocal effects.
modes.sound: The modeled all-buttons-in state pumps hard and produces substantially more distortion.
modes.watch_for: Treat it as a special effect; level-match and blend before assuming more is better.

sources.title: Softube FET Compressor Mk II manual

groups.summary: The switch changes the saturator itself, not merely the amount of color.

modes.name: Hrmc Off
modes.choose_for: Peak shaving, harder density, and output-stage-style solid-state clipping.
modes.sound: Subtle until the signal reaches the clip point, then increasingly obvious.
modes.watch_for: Use section bypasses to prove the density is not compressor movement.

modes.name: Hrmc On
modes.choose_for: Smooth harmonic enhancement that should read as richer rather than clipped.
modes.sound: A tapered overtone structure designed to add harmonics without obvious breakup.
modes.watch_for: Added brightness or loudness can masquerade as better glue; output-match it.

groups.summary: Choose the detector topology before deciding how much vintage color to retain.

modes.name: Classic
modes.choose_for: Variable-mu-style bloom, feedback movement, and program-dependent vintage behavior.
modes.sound: Softer, more interactive compression whose coloration changes with Calibration.
modes.watch_for: Low end and release behavior can become the event rather than transparent control.

modes.name: Modern
modes.choose_for: Cleaner feed-forward control while still using the transformer and tube stages.
modes.sound: More explicit, less colored gain reduction with less compression-dependent distortion.
modes.watch_for: Do not expect Calibration to behave like a generic age control in this mode.

groups.summary: Calibration changes compression-dependent push-pull crossover distortion in Classic mode.

modes.name: Clean
modes.choose_for: The 670 envelope with the least extra crossover grit.
modes.sound: Cleaner and more open than the nominal modeled condition.
modes.watch_for: Transformer and tube-stage controls can still color the path.

modes.name: Nominal
modes.choose_for: The expected healthy-hardware balance of movement and coloration.
modes.sound: The reference amount of modeled compression-linked distortion.
modes.watch_for: Judge it at the same gain reduction as the other states.

modes.name: Worn
modes.choose_for: Audible antique density, rougher buses, and intentionally aged program material.
modes.sound: Substantially more distortion tied to the compressor’s action.
modes.watch_for: It can cloud low mids quickly when reduction is already deep.

groups.summary: Two complete Softube model generations share the current interface.

modes.name: Mk I
modes.choose_for: The earlier Softube model’s familiar tone or deliberate continuity with that sound.
modes.sound: The legacy generation, not merely a darker preset of Mk II.
modes.watch_for: It does not make the current plug-in a drop-in substitute for old Mk I sessions.

modes.name: Mk II
modes.choose_for: New work and the later ground-up remodel with current workflow features.
modes.sound: Softube’s newer component model and present-day default CL 1B character.
modes.watch_for: Compare at matched gain reduction; the movement matters more than output level.

groups.summary: The combined position is a genuinely different program-dependent timing system.

modes.name: Fixed
modes.choose_for: Fast, simple peak control on drums and other percussive sources.
modes.sound: A fixed 1 ms attack and 50 ms release.
modes.watch_for: It can be too abrupt for exposed sustained phrases.

modes.name: Manual
modes.choose_for: Vocals, bass, piano, guitar, and any source needing authored attack and release.
modes.sound: Both timing controls work conventionally across their full ranges.
modes.watch_for: A setting that flatters one phrase may recover poorly on another.

modes.name: Fixed / Manual
modes.choose_for: Program material with both short peaks and longer phrases.
modes.sound: Fast fixed attack and a two-stage release that hands off to the manual Release setting.
modes.watch_for: Here Attack sets the release handoff delay; it is no longer an attack control.

groups.summary: The three curves cover different EMI-derived timing roles; THD removes gain reduction but keeps the audio path.

modes.name: Comp 1
modes.choose_for: Gentle mix-bus or subgroup glue and slower, RS124-inspired movement.
modes.sound: A 2:1 curve with slower time constants and the softest behavior of the three.
modes.watch_for: Deep reduction can still darken or thicken the program despite the gentle ratio.

modes.name: Comp 2
modes.choose_for: Punchier control that keeps Comp 1’s curve but recovers more quickly.
modes.sound: A modern middle state: Comp 1-like compression with release behavior nearer Limit.
modes.watch_for: Faster recovery can become audible on low-frequency-heavy material.

modes.name: Limit
modes.choose_for: Firm peak containment, forward drums, and the fastest Fairchild-inspired response.
modes.sound: The quickest and most assertive limiting curve.
modes.watch_for: Use the sidechain filter if bass makes the action too aggressive.

modes.name: THD
modes.choose_for: Using the Zener’s transistor path as a dedicated color stage.
modes.sound: The limiter threshold is disengaged while signal still traverses the complete audio path.
modes.watch_for: Input gain, impedance, and level now determine tone without a reduction meter to explain it.

sources.title: Softube Chandler Limited Zener Limiter manual

groups.summary: Choose the diode network and knee character first, then use Ratio to fine-tune the result.

modes.name: R Soft
modes.choose_for: Mastering, stereo buses, or the least audible compression artifacts.
modes.sound: The most neutral and gentle resistance-based curve.
modes.watch_for: It supplies less of the diode color that makes the other settings distinctive.

modes.name: Germ Soft
modes.choose_for: General use, buses, bass, and drums needing smooth color with preserved attack.
modes.sound: A gentle single-germanium knee with mild character.
modes.watch_for: Its softness can invite more reduction than the arrangement needs.

modes.name: Germ Med
modes.choose_for: More punch and color while retaining the forgiving germanium family.
modes.sound: A sharper five-diode germanium curve with additional vibe.
modes.watch_for: Revisit Ratio after switching; Curve and Ratio are intentionally interactive.

modes.name: Silicon Med
modes.choose_for: A firmer knee and different tonal edge without reaching the hardest states.
modes.sound: Sharper than Germ Med with a distinct silicon character.
modes.watch_for: Transient definition can turn into hardness on bright close mics.

modes.name: Silicon Hard
modes.choose_for: Parallel submix smash and clearly audible envelope shaping.
modes.sound: A hard two-silicon-diode knee with pronounced character.
modes.watch_for: Blend or constrain it; full-wet use can flatten the front of a bus.

modes.name: Zener Hard
modes.choose_for: The most extreme crush, hard parallel effects, and deliberate attitude.
modes.sound: The sharpest knee and the most different character in the selector.
modes.watch_for: Small control changes can become large audible changes at this end of the range.

sources.title: Softube Chandler Limited Germanium Compressor manual

groups.summary: Start with the main job, then choose how the detector should react.

modes.name: Limit
modes.choose_for: Squashing drums, catching peaks, ducking, or the unit’s stranger negative-ratio effects.
modes.sound: Gain falls above Threshold; the detector and source switches determine how conventionally.
modes.watch_for: Gate detector in Limit creates extreme 1:-20 behavior, not a normal limiter.

modes.name: Expand
modes.choose_for: Noise gating, dynamic expansion, keyed rhythms, and opening space below Threshold.
modes.sound: Gain falls below Threshold, from soft expansion to hard gating.
modes.watch_for: Use Range to avoid turning natural decay into abrupt silence.

groups.summary: Detector Type changes attack behavior and, in Gate, the actual ratio.

modes.name: Avg
modes.choose_for: Smoother limiting, punch from preserved transients, and natural soft gating.
modes.sound: A slower, complex 1–15 ms attack using Valley’s averaging detector.
modes.watch_for: The fastest peaks can escape and reach the modeled output clipping.

modes.name: Peak
modes.choose_for: Fast transient limiting, longer snare tails, or tighter soft gating.
modes.sound: Roughly 50 µs attack with more conventional peak behavior.
modes.watch_for: It can sound more distorted or abrupt than Avg on full program material.

modes.name: Gate
modes.choose_for: Hard gates in Expand or broken, inverted-envelope effects in Limit.
modes.sound: A 1:20 gate below threshold—or an extreme 1:-20 negative limiter above it.
modes.watch_for: Longer Release and restricted Range are often essential to control pops and crackle.

groups.summary: Styles are problem-specific multiband designs; audition at low Amount and chain only complementary jobs.

modes.name: Clarity 1
modes.choose_for: Immediate separation and definition on a generally congested mix.
modes.sound: A direct clarity lift intended to be used gently.
modes.watch_for: It can become an over-processed sheen when the mix is already open.

modes.name: Clarity 2
modes.choose_for: Midrange definition when the top also needs some harshness control.
modes.sound: More focus through the mids with simultaneous high-frequency taming.
modes.watch_for: Do not mistake reduced harshness for a universally better tonal balance.

modes.name: Neutral
modes.choose_for: A strong mix that needs only restrained polish.
modes.sound: The least directional S73 style with gentle sheen.
modes.watch_for: If it seems inactive, that may be the correct result; do not force Amount.

modes.name: Gentle Comp
modes.choose_for: Glue and density without choosing crossover and timing settings manually.
modes.sound: Broad multiband cohesion rather than a tonal repair.
modes.watch_for: Softube suggests keeping gain reduction around 3 dB.

modes.name: More Air
modes.choose_for: A mix that needs breathing room and controllable top-end sheen.
modes.sound: Amount controls the air treatment; the Air switch adds still more sheen.
modes.watch_for: Level-match carefully—top lift can win comparisons at first listen.

modes.name: De-Rumble
modes.choose_for: Low-frequency rumble or mud that obscures the rest of the mix.
modes.sound: Low-end cleanup with improved overall definition.
modes.watch_for: Follow with Clarity only if a second, different problem remains.

modes.name: Punch
modes.choose_for: Kick and bass that need firmer definition and impact.
modes.sound: A low-end-focused punch treatment rather than general loudness.
modes.watch_for: It cannot repair kick/bass arrangement conflicts by itself.

modes.name: Wide Mix
modes.choose_for: Gentle expansion of an already coherent stereo mix.
modes.sound: A controlled stereo widening treatment.
modes.watch_for: Spatial styles are not compatible with mono or multi-mono versions.

modes.name: Ambience
modes.choose_for: Bringing forward room tone and existing spatial detail.
modes.sound: More audible ambience rather than simple left-right expansion.
modes.watch_for: Noise, reverb buildup, and cymbal wash can rise with the desired room.

modes.name: Vocals Enhance
modes.choose_for: Moving a lead vocal forward from within a stereo mix.
modes.sound: A spatially informed emphasis of the central vocal presence.
modes.watch_for: It is not a substitute for stem-level vocal automation or repair.

groups.summary: Style processing happens before the final brick-wall limiter; Parallel Mix does not bypass that limiter.

modes.name: Transparent
modes.choose_for: The least invasive loudness and control path.
modes.sound: The most restrained of the five mastering styles.
modes.watch_for: Limiter Gain is a separate downstream decision; do not hide excessive Style processing with it.

modes.name: Loud
modes.choose_for: High-RMS production references and deliberately dense masters.
modes.sound: The style most explicitly aimed at average loudness.
modes.watch_for: Compare punch and tonal balance at matched playback level.

modes.name: Punch
modes.choose_for: Adding weight and impact before final limiting.
modes.sound: More perceived punch and body than Transparent.
modes.watch_for: Too much Amount can turn transient emphasis into limiter workload.

modes.name: Wide
modes.choose_for: A stereo master that needs more dimensional spread.
modes.sound: M/S processing produces a wider, more three-dimensional presentation.
modes.watch_for: It is not compatible with mono or multi-mono instances.

modes.name: Deess
modes.choose_for: Master-bus sibilance, brittle cymbals, or broader high-frequency containment.
modes.sound: An M/S-aware all-round de-essing algorithm usable in mixing or mastering.
modes.watch_for: If the harshness is localized, Weiss Deess offers more explicit control.

groups.summary: The two hidden hardware variants change whether emphasis reaches saturation, compression, or both.

modes.name: HF
modes.choose_for: The original tape-like CompSat warmth and high-frequency peak softening.
modes.sound: High frequencies hit the saturation harder while compression behavior stays unchanged.
modes.watch_for: In 1:1, this is still an active soft-clipping color even without compression.

modes.name: HF2
modes.choose_for: Stronger high-frequency control when bright material should trigger compression as well.
modes.sound: The HF emphasis reaches the whole CompSat circuit, including the detector behavior.
modes.watch_for: Sibilance and cymbals can drive more reduction than in HF.

modes.name: LF
modes.choose_for: Preserving more high-frequency openness while controlling lower-frequency energy.
modes.sound: Highs are attenuated into the detector, so they trigger less compression.
modes.watch_for: Low-frequency events may dominate the envelope if the source is bass-heavy.

sources.title: Softube Empirical Labs Mike-E Comp manual

groups.summary: Each mode changes hidden multiband compression, timing, de-essing, EQ, and sometimes width; start at Amount zero.

modes.name: Vocal Clarify
modes.choose_for: A vocal that needs low-end control, articulation, and reduced masking.
modes.sound: Moderate de-essing and clarity EQ around a controlled low end.
modes.watch_for: Add post High Band only after the de-essing behavior is right.

modes.name: Vocal Focus
modes.choose_for: A lead that must stay firmly forward through a dense production.
modes.sound: Harder, higher-ratio compression with de-essing and mid-presence emphasis.
modes.watch_for: The extra focus can overstate breath, nasal tone, or room noise.

modes.name: Mix Bus
modes.choose_for: General glue with more midrange punch and smoother spectral extremes.
modes.sound: Lows and highs settle while the center gains definition.
modes.watch_for: Reject it if it wins only by making the mix seem brighter or denser.

modes.name: Mix Bus Wide
modes.choose_for: A stereo mix that needs width and a cleaner middle.
modes.sound: A wider presentation with less central congestion.
modes.watch_for: Check mono and make sure the lead remains anchored.

modes.name: Drum Bus
modes.choose_for: Glue, less boxiness, and a little more midrange hit on a kit.
modes.sound: A denser drum envelope with tuned tonal cleanup.
modes.watch_for: Use Dry/Wet to restore attacks before changing the hidden envelope with more Amount.

modes.name: Bass Instruments
modes.choose_for: Uneven bass, synth bass, or low strings needing richness plus articulation.
modes.sound: A more even low end with luxurious weight and some midrange clarity.
modes.watch_for: It can make already-layered bass occupy too much low-mid space.

modes.name: Keys / Guitar
modes.choose_for: Piano, Rhodes, synths, or individual guitars needing glue and presence.
modes.sound: Coordinated compression and presence enhancement for harmonic instruments.
modes.watch_for: Chords can expose multiband movement more readily than single notes.

modes.name: Stereo Guitars Wide
modes.choose_for: Hard-panned guitar pairs or keyboard buses needing extra span and clarity.
modes.sound: More width, presence, and high-end definition across the stereo pair.
modes.watch_for: It assumes meaningful left-right content; mono or near-mono sources are a poor fit.

groups.summary: Softube does not license or identify the machines; these are producer-facing character choices, not confirmed hardware claims.

modes.name: A
modes.choose_for: Mastering-scale cohesion, clean buses, and the most linear starting point.
modes.sound: The cleanest and most restrained type, with the least obvious tape personality.
modes.watch_for: Match THD and output before comparing; clean can lose to louder in a quick A/B.

modes.name: B
modes.choose_for: The recognizable tape feel most producers want while keeping the effect controlled.
modes.sound: More audible weight and machine identity than A without jumping straight to vintage coloration.
modes.watch_for: Transformer-like low-end weight can accumulate across many instances.

modes.name: C
modes.choose_for: Deliberate vintage color, softened bandwidth, and obviously aged tone.
modes.sound: The strongest old-machine impression of the three.
modes.watch_for: It is a character choice, not the automatic answer for every mix bus.

groups.summary: Choose the nonlinear family first, then use Character, Dynamics, filters, and blend to fit it.

modes.name: Solid
modes.choose_for: Vocals, drums, and tracks that need definition and separation.
modes.sound: Early-1970s-inspired solid-state color that helps a source stand out in the soundstage.
modes.watch_for: Forward definition can become brittle on already aggressive transients.

modes.name: Transf
modes.choose_for: Kick, bass, full mixes, and material that benefits from American-console low-end weight.
modes.sound: Transformer-inspired density with a strong low-frequency signature.
modes.watch_for: The foundation can thicken before the midrange actually improves.

modes.name: Master
modes.choose_for: Buses and masters needing subtle analog touch while preserving transients.
modes.sound: Smooth mastering-oriented saturation whose Drive changes harmonic content as well as amount.
modes.watch_for: There is no single neutral Drive position; search for the program-specific sweet spot.

modes.name: Tube
modes.choose_for: Bass and guitar that need warm, mid-1960s boutique tube character.
modes.sound: Rounded tube warmth that Softube specifically recommends for bass and guitar.
modes.watch_for: Low-mid warmth can reduce apparent articulation when the arrangement is already dense.

modes.name: Modern
modes.choose_for: Immediate warmth and punch with a more contemporary all-valve distortion voice.
modes.sound: An English modern triode-inspired character that becomes audible quickly.
modes.watch_for: Its instant punch can overstate sources that already have a hard front edge.

groups.summary: The labels describe what is protected, not the band being saturated.

modes.name: Keep Low
modes.choose_for: Bass, kick, and loops whose low-end envelope must remain recognizable.
modes.sound: Higher frequencies saturate more while the bottom stays comparatively intact.
modes.watch_for: Do not read the label backward; this is not a low-band distortion mode.

modes.name: Neutral
modes.choose_for: Simple full-band thickening when neither extreme needs special protection.
modes.sound: A more even distribution of saturation across the spectrum.
modes.watch_for: Both low-end fuzz and high-end hardness can arrive together.

modes.name: Keep High
modes.choose_for: Bright percussion, vocals, and sources whose top-end detail must remain clear.
modes.sound: Lower frequencies saturate more while the highs stay comparatively intact.
modes.watch_for: Preserved brightness can conceal too much low-mid distortion in solo.

groups.summary: Re-adjust Input when comparing: each profile reaches a similar amount of bending at a different level.

modes.name: Classic M-A-S
modes.choose_for: General mix or bus energy with fundamentals left relatively unclipped.
modes.sound: Harmonics focus through the mids and upper range while the foundation stays steadier.
modes.watch_for: Color begins below the first saturation LED; an unlit meter is not necessarily neutral.

modes.name: Low Bandwidth
modes.choose_for: Broken-speaker drums, narrow grit, and deliberately constrained lo-fi material.
modes.sound: Highs and lows distort first while the mids remain comparatively unaffected.
modes.watch_for: The hollowed mid behavior can make a source sound smaller rather than simply dirtier.

modes.name: Low Presence
modes.choose_for: Vocals and instruments that need upper-mid clarity and articulation.
modes.sound: The saturation emphasis brings forward the vocal-presence region.
modes.watch_for: Sibilance and pick noise can become the first thing the ear notices.

modes.name: High Presence
modes.choose_for: Air, shimmer, and a more elevated high-frequency polish.
modes.sound: Emphasis moves above Low Presence into the lower-treble / air region.
modes.watch_for: Use Dual and 2nd sparingly if the added brightness becomes brittle.

modes.name: Bass Distortion
modes.choose_for: Bass-heavy sources needing transformer-like low-end color or deliberate thinning.
modes.sound: The bass distorts while the highs stay comparatively unaffected.
modes.watch_for: Softube notes that it can thin the bass even while adding low-frequency character.

modes.name: Treble Distortion
modes.choose_for: Smoothing harsh transients and rough edges with a tape-like high-frequency bias.
modes.sound: High frequencies bend more than the rest of the signal.
modes.watch_for: Too much can turn useful attack into dullness before the body gains enough color.

groups.summary: One Brain effect runs at a time after the core bit mutation, sample-rate reduction, and analog-modeled filter.

modes.name: Wave
modes.choose_for: Radical distortion, octave effects, bit swaps, or input-tracking synthesized waveforms.
modes.sound: Eight shapers range from rectification and folding to tracked saw and square waves.
modes.watch_for: Tracking modes need enough Drive; begin with all eight data bits in their normal state.

modes.name: Delay
modes.choose_for: Lo-fi echoes from gentle repeats to screaming feedback.
modes.sound: An 8-bit stereo delay whose degraded path can interact with the clock and filter.
modes.watch_for: Sample-rate reduction and filtering apply only to the delayed signal in this mode.

modes.name: Pitch
modes.choose_for: Crude harmonies, chorus-like detune, and shifts from two octaves down to one up.
modes.sound: A short-buffer 8-bit mono shifter returned to both outputs.
modes.watch_for: Clock reduction and bit mutation can turn it into a pitch-shifting delay rather than clean transposition.

modes.name: Step
modes.choose_for: Tempo-synced rhythmic filtering, gates, and deterministic or random filter patterns.
modes.sound: An eight-step multimode-filter sequencer with Freeze, Forward, Alternating, and Random motion.
modes.watch_for: Use DAW sync for exact tempo; free-running mode shares the delay clock.

groups.summary: Choose the physical playback perspective before adding Drive, Width, or parallel blend.

modes.name: Portable Radio
modes.choose_for: The smallest, most collapsed lo-fi cue and obvious vocal or drum filtering.
modes.sound: The most fragile speaker response; it falls apart dramatically when driven.
modes.watch_for: It can remove too much body to work as more than a parallel or automated effect.

modes.name: Cassette Deck
modes.choose_for: 1980s boombox tone, snarly mids, and a lo-fi sound that retains useful bass.
modes.sound: Tighter low end and a more aggressive midrange bite than Portable Radio.
modes.watch_for: The bite can pile up around vocals and guitars in an already mid-forward mix.

modes.name: Hi-Fi Speaker
modes.choose_for: Subtle speaker-in-room perspective and the most flexible starting point.
modes.sound: A genuinely good speaker response in a room rather than an obviously broken device.
modes.watch_for: Width and intermediate Dry/Wet settings can make placement ambiguous; check mono.

groups.summary: Choose the ELI circuit first; the meter changes from THD to gain reduction in Distress.

modes.name: Toasty
modes.choose_for: Subtle warmth and colorful density below roughly 10–14% THD.
modes.sound: The warm saturation circuit from Mike-E’s CompSat section.
modes.watch_for: At heavy Drive the distinction from Crunchy becomes less informative.

modes.name: Crunchy
modes.choose_for: Harder breakup and shaving transients from drums or other percussive material.
modes.sound: Mike-E preamp distortion with a firmer, crunchier edge than Toasty.
modes.watch_for: The extra edge can read as level or presence unless output-matched.

modes.name: Distress
modes.choose_for: Forward vocals, controlled snares, or brutally crushed parallel drums.
modes.sound: Distressor/Mike-E compression at its fastest, most aggressive setting.
modes.watch_for: The meter now reads gain reduction; 3–5 dB is already a meaningful starting range.

groups.summary: This second selector applies Empirical Labs-style emphasis around the chosen distortion circuit.

modes.name: XFRM
modes.choose_for: Transformer-like weight and more distortion emphasis in the low end.
modes.sound: The nonlinear focus shifts downward.
modes.watch_for: Bass buildup can obscure the envelope you chose with the Distortion selector.

modes.name: Wide
modes.choose_for: The broadest, most even distortion bandwidth.
modes.sound: A wide-range tonal treatment without deliberate low- or high-end emphasis.
modes.watch_for: Full-band density can expose noise and room tone along with the wanted source.

modes.name: Tape
modes.choose_for: Smoother top-end emphasis and a tape-like way of rounding rough punch.
modes.sound: The distortion focus shifts toward the high frequencies.
modes.watch_for: Too much can soften articulation before the body is sufficiently altered.

groups.summary: The modes choose the mathematical overtone generator; Adaptive usually keeps each one in its intended sweet spot.

modes.name: Soft
modes.choose_for: The safest all-round excitement on instruments, buses, and masters.
modes.sound: A very soft knee with a smooth, broad spectrum of harmonics.
modes.watch_for: Its easy transition can encourage more processing than the mix needs.

modes.name: Hard
modes.choose_for: A firmer, more obvious edge while retaining a broad overtone spectrum.
modes.sound: A slightly harder knee than Soft with many harmonics.
modes.watch_for: Watch the Harmonics LED; constant red means hard clipping rather than elegant excitation.

modes.name: Poly 3
modes.choose_for: Very transparent third-harmonic emphasis and precise mastering work.
modes.sound: Only third harmonics are generated inside the non-clipping range.
modes.watch_for: The transition into clipping is less smooth than Soft or Hard.

modes.name: Poly 5
modes.choose_for: Transparent third- and fifth-harmonic structure with slightly more complexity.
modes.sound: Third and fifth harmonics dominate until the generator clips.
modes.watch_for: Keep Adaptive on unless you specifically want only loud events to excite.

groups.summary: The current manual exposes seven algorithms, including Chamber. Do not automate the selector.

modes.name: Spring
modes.choose_for: Guitars and obvious character where a limited-bandwidth spring belongs in the arrangement.
modes.sound: Bright and unmistakable, between a tape-echo spring and a cleaner studio tank.
modes.watch_for: Use Bright instead of Full when the richer low end is too much; avoid full mixes.

modes.name: Plate
modes.choose_for: Vocals and drums needing dense, dark, immediately recognizable depth.
modes.sound: Choose Digital for the early classic digital-plate design or Analog for modeled mechanical resonance.
modes.watch_for: Analog Bright, Medium, and Dark change onset and decay character; this is not one generic plate.

modes.name: Room
modes.choose_for: Dense, versatile studio ambience, shorter spaces, and buses that need depth without a long tail.
modes.sound: A smaller, denser variation of the 224-derived Concert Hall design with less pronounced echoes.
modes.watch_for: Its modulation can sound pitchy on piano; System Noise models internal quantization artifacts.

modes.name: Concert Hall
modes.choose_for: Lush vocals, strings, pads, and other non-percussive sources needing a sparse ethereal tail.
modes.sound: The chorus-like 224-derived hall associated with long, beautifully modulated space.
modes.watch_for: Pitch modulation can become seasick or unstable on exposed piano and other tuned attacks.

modes.name: Random Hall
modes.choose_for: Open, clear, expensive-feeling depth on almost any source.
modes.sound: 480-derived spatialization with Size decoupled from Time in Effect mode.
modes.watch_for: Many parameter combinations are intentionally less forgiving; start from a preset.

modes.name: Cathedral
modes.choose_for: Pads, synths, shimmer, and long synthetic tails unconcerned with room realism.
modes.sound: A lush, modulated wash that diffuses pitch over long decays.
modes.watch_for: Percussive drums can disappear into its long, noise-like tail.

modes.name: Chamber
modes.choose_for: Short drum rooms, buses, or long tails that should preserve pitch.
modes.sound: Maximally dense and modulated without audible pitch artifacts; Flat, Chamber A, and B set tone.
modes.watch_for: Freeze buffers do not save with the project; print or automate the gesture.

groups.summary: Five curated algorithms share one control set; do not automate the selector.

modes.name: Spring
modes.choose_for: Guitars and obvious vintage flavor without the full Dimensions editing surface.
modes.sound: A bright tape-echo-derived spring, neither amp-tank dirty nor pristine studio clean.
modes.watch_for: Its 7.5 kHz bandwidth makes it a character decision, not a neutral full-mix room.

modes.name: Plate Digital
modes.choose_for: Warm, lush vocals and guitars with early-digital plate identity.
modes.sound: A recreation of the first commercial digital reverb’s constrained but beautiful design.
modes.watch_for: It is not the cleanest option and is not intended for a whole mix.

modes.name: Plate Analog
modes.choose_for: Dark, dense vocals and drums with a modeled mechanical onset.
modes.sound: Resonance modeling supplies plate-like attack and a carefully tuned mechanical tail.
modes.watch_for: The dense low-mid energy can crowd a full mix.

modes.name: Synth Hall
modes.choose_for: Long pads, synths, anti-shimmer, and abstract ambient wash.
modes.sound: The lush Cathedral algorithm from Dimensions, improved for long synthetic diffusion.
modes.watch_for: Avoid drums when pitch diffusion and long bloom obscure the pulse.

modes.name: Chamber
modes.choose_for: Short drum depth, buses, and long reverb that should retain tonal center.
modes.sound: Dense, immediate, maximally modulated space without audible pitch artifacts.
modes.watch_for: Width can mute the mid at maximum; verify the center and mono sum.

groups.summary: Filter slope decides whether lowering Sample Rate becomes bandwidth reduction or audible foldback.

modes.name: 48 dB
modes.choose_for: A cleaner vocal plate or darker digital reverb with the fewest aliasing artifacts.
modes.sound: The steepest anti-alias filter makes Sample Rate behave most like a low-pass limit.
modes.watch_for: The early-digital bandwidth remains; clean here does not mean full-frequency modern reverb.

modes.name: 24 dB
modes.choose_for: A middle ground between controlled bandwidth and audible converter personality.
modes.sound: More foldback than 48 dB without the obvious damage of the shallowest settings.
modes.watch_for: Judge on sustained tails, where atonal artifacts are easier to hear.

modes.name: 12 dB
modes.choose_for: Crunchy snares, robotic tails, and audible early-converter character.
modes.sound: A shallow filter lets more above-Nyquist energy fold back into the reverb.
modes.watch_for: The added high-frequency content is atonal, not a conventional brightness boost.

modes.name: Off
modes.choose_for: Maximum aliasing, sound design, and the most deliberately broken converter behavior.
modes.sound: Unfiltered foldback becomes part of the tail as Sample Rate falls.
modes.watch_for: Monitor level and high-frequency fatigue; this is a destruction mode, not a neutral plate.

groups.summary: Every mode changes the feedback character, modulation behavior, and the controls exposed around the same tap pattern.

modes.name: Filter
modes.choose_for: Cleanly composed tap rhythms with deliberate alternating low- and high-pass behavior.
modes.sound: A normal delay whose tap filters range from all-low-pass to all-high-pass patterns.
modes.watch_for: Filter contrast can become the rhythm; make sure the actual tap timing still works.

modes.name: Reverb
modes.choose_for: Living echoes, diffuse clusters, and tap patterns that should cross into algorithmic space.
modes.sound: FDN-oriented pitch and amplitude modulation plus diffusion in the feedback loop.
modes.watch_for: High diffusion consumes mix energy quickly even when individual taps seem quiet.

modes.name: BBD
modes.choose_for: Clocked bucket-brigade grit, darker repeats, and pitch movement tied to delay time.
modes.sound: Longer delay lowers the modeled clock rate, increasing aliasing and changing playback pitch.
modes.watch_for: Automating time moves audio already in the delay line; print intentionally.

modes.name: Tape
modes.choose_for: Drive, dirt, wobble, and a more performable mechanical feedback loop.
modes.sound: Tape-style degradation with drive that strongly affects feedback behavior.
modes.watch_for: Feedback can rise dramatically as Drive increases.

modes.name: Pan
modes.choose_for: Rhythmic stereo motion with controlled waveform, speed, and amount.
modes.sound: A useful preset phase relationship animates the taps across the panorama.
modes.watch_for: Movement can distract from the source if every tap crosses the center.

modes.name: Lo-Fi
modes.choose_for: Organic degraded repeats and evolving sound-design returns.
modes.sound: Bit crushing plus resonant four-pole filtering driven by an envelope follower.
modes.watch_for: Resonance and envelope motion can create sudden spectral peaks.

groups.summary: The original hardware allowed one speed at a time; the plug-in preserves that limitation.

modes.name: I
modes.choose_for: Lush, slower widening on pads, guitars, bass parallels, and restrained 1980s color.
modes.sound: The slower of the two fixed modulation speeds.
modes.watch_for: High input can distort the modeled chorus stage; use that deliberately.

modes.name: II
modes.choose_for: More animated chorus, fills, and parts that need a faster audible shimmer.
modes.sound: A faster modulation rate with more obvious movement.
modes.watch_for: It can pitch-wobble exposed sustained notes more readily than Mode I.

groups.summary: The first five come from Widener; Slow Mod is Layers’ extra chorus-derived option.

modes.name: Classic
modes.choose_for: Predictable mono-to-stereo widening when a little delay-based character is acceptable.
modes.sound: Mid-derived delayed sides with the center left untouched.
modes.watch_for: Left/right comb filtering and audible echo can appear on percussive sources.

modes.name: Frequency Spread
modes.choose_for: Percussive or upper-frequency width with fewer obvious echoes than Classic.
modes.sound: Phase shifts move energy into the sides while leaving the mid untouched.
modes.watch_for: Low frequencies can appear panned; raise the Low Frequency boundary.

modes.name: Rotation
modes.choose_for: Natural mono-source width without changing left/right frequency response.
modes.sound: Phase rotation creates a smooth image but dips the mid near Emphasis.
modes.watch_for: It softens transients and does little for an already-stereo source.

modes.name: Ambience
modes.choose_for: Guitars, drums, and layers that should feel bigger as well as wider.
modes.sound: A short reverb-like network adds cross-channel ambience.
modes.watch_for: Lower High Frequency if it turns tinny.

modes.name: Reflections
modes.choose_for: Stereo enlargement with echo patterns shuffled to reduce obvious chorusing.
modes.sound: Dense short reflections mask comb filtering and audible pitch movement.
modes.watch_for: It changes both mid/side and left/right information; mono-check the whole sum.

modes.name: Slow Mod
modes.choose_for: Syrupy, thick chorus width rather than artifact-minimizing stereo conversion.
modes.sound: A hardware-rack-inspired slow modulation effect with three intensity speeds.
modes.watch_for: It is the most overtly chorus-like choice; use Wet Only when the center must remain stable.

groups.summary: Every method places its unavoidable stereo artifacts somewhere different; choose the least damaging tradeoff.

modes.name: Classic
modes.choose_for: Predictable mono widening and strong apparent spread from a simple source.
modes.sound: Delay-derived sides leave the mid untouched and collapse cleanly to mono.
modes.watch_for: Left/right comb filtering and slap can be audible; adjust Size and darken the added signal.

modes.name: Frequency Spread
modes.choose_for: Percussive sounds and upper-mid/high widening without audible echoes.
modes.sound: Phase spreading leaves the mid untouched and is smoother than Classic.
modes.watch_for: Low frequencies can pull toward one side; raise Low Frequency.

modes.name: Rotation
modes.choose_for: A natural-feeling mono source, especially snare, with no left/right EQ change.
modes.sound: Phase rotation widens while introducing a soft dip in the mid at Emphasis.
modes.watch_for: Avoid important mono elements at Emphasis; it also softens transients.

modes.name: Ambience
modes.choose_for: Drum buses, guitars, and tracks that should gain both width and a sense of space.
modes.sound: A very short reverb-like figure-eight network crosses energy between channels.
modes.watch_for: It can sound tinny; lower High Frequency and adjust Size.

modes.name: Reflections
modes.choose_for: The most reverb-like widening with reduced audible echo and chorusing.
modes.sound: Shuffled short reflections mask comb-filter artifacts across the stereo field.
modes.watch_for: It alters the mid as well as the sides; use the meters and verify mono.
